skill.name: image-to-video
skill.description: Guide for turning still images into videos with inference.sh models, including model choice, motion prompts, camera movement, and workflow tips.
skill.summary: Create image-to-video prompts and choose suitable models for realistic or stylized motion.
skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: The critical confirmed issue is the quick-start command that pipes https://cli.inference.sh directly into sh. Most medium backtick findings are Markdown formatting, model identifiers, or visible infsh examples without hidden execution. The related npx install examples add supply-chain risk, so safer installation guidance is needed before publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the quick-start command with manual download, checksum verification, and an explicit shell invocation after review.

remediation.issue: Related skills are installed through npx commands.
remediation.suggestion: Link to reviewed marketplace pages or require users to inspect package sources before installing related skills.

remediation.issue: External CLI use sends media and prompts to network services.
remediation.suggestion: State the required domains, authentication flow, and data shared with inference.sh before command examples.

content.value_statement: Static images often need motion for social, product, or presentation use. This skill guides model choice, motion prompts, and workflow steps for image-to-video generation.
actual_capabilities: Compares image-to-video models for realistic, stylized, fabric, and general animation needs.
Provides prompt patterns for camera movement, subject motion, atmosphere, and pacing.
Gives scenario prompts for landscapes, portraits, products, fabric scenes, and architecture.
Explains clip duration choices and when to stitch shorter outputs.
Shows a still-image, animation, upscale, audio, and merge workflow using inference.sh.
Lists common mistakes that cause artifacts, distortion, or chaotic motion.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and access to the referenced video models.
Provides guidance, not a bundled video generation engine.
Quality depends on source image resolution, model behavior, and prompt clarity.
The quick-start install command includes a remote shell pipeline that needs safer replacement.

use_cases.title: Social Video Clips
use_cases.description: Turn campaign stills into short clips with subtle motion and clear camera direction.

use_cases.title: Product Motion Tests
use_cases.description: Choose a model and prompt style for product, fabric, or reflective object animation.

use_cases.title: Creative Video Prototypes
use_cases.description: Plan image generation, animation, upscaling, audio, and merge steps for a polished short video.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Landscape Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me animate this landscape image. Recommend a model and write a short prompt with subtle water, cloud, and light motion.

prompt_templates.title: Choose The Right Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the available image-to-video models for my image type: [describe image]. Choose one model and explain the motion style.

prompt_templates.title: Product Motion Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an image-to-video prompt for a product shot. Include one camera move, subtle reflections, and a smooth premium pace.

prompt_templates.title: Full Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a complete still-to-video workflow for [goal]. Include source image preparation, animation, upscaling, audio, stitching, and quality checks.

output_examples.input: A fashion product image with flowing fabric.
output_examples.output: Recommended model: Fabric 1.0. Motion should emphasize gentle cloth ripples, restrained camera movement, and short clip length.

output_examples.input: A portrait that needs a subtle animated social clip.
output: Use Wan 2.5 i2v for face fidelity.
Prompt for breathing, blinking, soft hair movement, and stable camera framing.
Keep the clip near four seconds.

output_examples.input: A landscape image that should become a looping background.
output_examples.output: Use subtle water, cloud, and light movement. Keep camera motion slow and limit duration for a cleaner loop.

best_practices: Request subtle motion before dramatic action.
Choose the model based on subject type and desired motion style.
Keep clips short, then stitch multiple clips when longer duration is needed.
anti_patterns: Do not combine multiple conflicting camera directions in one prompt.
Do not ask for complex action scenes from a single still image.
Do not start from low-resolution source images when quality matters.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps turn still images into short videos using model selection and motion prompting guidance.

faq.question: Does the skill generate video by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides use of inference.sh models and CLI workflows for video generation.

faq.question: Which model is best for realistic motion?
faq.answer: The guide recommends Wan 2.5 i2v for realistic motion and face fidelity.

faq.question: Which model should I use for fabric or liquid motion?
faq.answer: The guide recommends Fabric 1.0 for cloth, fabric, liquid, and flowing material scenes.

faq.question: How long should image-to-video clips be?
faq.answer: The guide recommends short clips, often two to five seconds, for higher quality results.

faq.question: Are there security concerns?
faq.answer: Yes. The current quick start pipes a remote installer into sh and should be replaced with verified manual steps.
